interpretations.mapping: Read the hall body (13 joints, 12 connections, one component — a tree) through the artifact's graph="tree" value. The passage's isolation event is operationalized as the single change cut="none" -> cut="bridge" at closure="open": _find_special elects the first edge whose removal raises the component count (_bridge_edge), the removal is applied, and the outcome is read from component_count() (prediction: 1 -> 2) and has_bridge() (prediction: true). The exiled small piece stands for the hand outside the connected part.
assumptions: Tree-ness is the operative property: in a connected graph with edges = nodes - 1, every edge is a bridge, so the artifact's 8-node, 7-edge tree is a fair reduced stand-in for the 13-joint, 12-edge body.
component_count() is the operative formalization of the final's phrase 'the body's connected part'.
Which bridge is elected does not matter for the question; _find_special's first-found convention (edge [0,1]) is acceptable.
exclusions: Does not model the reroute itself: the hall gesture removes AND re-attaches an endpoint in one release; cut only removes.
No cycle appears in this interpretation; the loop half of both passages is excluded.
Node identities (hand, head, elbow) and all geometry/positions are excluded; only connectivity is read.

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'that circuit' via the closure export: compare closure="open" against closure="returned" at graph="tree", cut="none", reading _bridge_edge/_chord_edge through has_bridge() and the cut="chord" pathway. The appended edge [4,7] ('crown to crown, around the trunk') creates the circuit; edges on it stop being bridges (a chord now exists, so cut="chord" removes something and component_count() stays 1), while the trunk edge [0,1] remains a bridge — the circuit protects the belonging of some parts and not others.
assumptions: Adding the return edge is a fair stand-in, for bridge-status purposes, for the hall's reroute to the head that closes a loop.
Bridge-status (is this edge solely responsible?) is the operative sense of a line 'reaching' a part.
exclusions: closure only ever adds an edge; nothing is exiled, so the passage's exile half (the hand outside the circuit) is not modeled here.
The demotion is read through _find_special and probe methods, not through what a visitor can see; legibility in the encounter is excluded.
graph="theta" (born bridgeless) is excluded as outside both passages.

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize the tutorial's learning element 'Prediction before editing' as a discrimination task with the artifact's built-in negative control: at graph="barbell", closure="open", compare cut="bridge" against cut="chord" — same gesture, two edges that look equally important — and read component_count() (prediction: 2 vs 1). The learner's written prediction of which edge is solely responsible, made before the cut, is the measured object.
assumptions: The bridge and a chord are visually on a par in the barbell rendering, so prediction cannot be read off the picture.
A failed prediction is an informative outcome, not a failed lesson.
exclusions: barbell is not a body; nothing maps to joints, the hand or edge 5.
Does not touch the final's loop or exile; closure is held at "open".
The verdict plate text (STILL CONNECTED / BROKEN) is treated as readout only, not as the measured change.

reference_fixture.description: Pen-and-paper component count for the tree shape under the bounded comparison, plus the closure demotion — pure graph arithmetic from the literals in bridge_cut.gd. These are labelled predictions: nothing has run under this record's identity.
constants_cited: tree node literal in _shape(): _pos has 8 Vector3 entries
expected: baseline: _chord_edge == -1, so a request for cut="chord" removes nothing and _verdict() returns "NO CHORD TO CUT\nevery edge is a bridge\nstill 1 piece"
after the single change cut="bridge": component_count() == 2, piece sizes 1 ({node 0}) and 7 ({nodes 1..7})
at closure="returned", cut="none": still 1 component; cycle rank = 1; _chord_edge == 1 (edge [1,2], first edge on the cycle); has_bridge() still true because [0,1], [2,5], [3,6] lie off the cycle
reference_fixture.arithmetic: Tree: 8 nodes, 7 edges. Connected with edges = nodes - 1 (7 = 8 - 1) => acyclic => one component and every edge a bridge. _find_special scans i = 0..6: removing i=0 ([0,1]) strands node 0, components 1 -> 2 > base, so _bridge_edge = 0; no removal keeps the count at base, so _chord_edge = -1. Single change cut="bridge": _removed = [0]; union-find over the remaining 6 edges chains 1-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, 3-6, 3-7 into one set of 7 and leaves {0}: _n_comp = 2, sizes 1 and 7. closure="returned" appends [4,7]: 8 edges on 8 nodes gives cycle rank 8 - 8 + 1 = 1; the cycle is 4-2-1-3-7-4 (edges [2,4],[1,2],[1,3],[3,7],[4,7]), so removing any one of those five leaves 1 component (first at i=1 => _chord_edge = 1), while removing [0,1], [2,5] or [3,6] still disconnects => has_bridge() remains true.

questions.question: Before releasing a rerouted endpoint, can the learner predict which of the body's twelve connections are solely responsible for it staying one piece — and reconstruct, by removal rather than by looking, how a single changed relation moves an edge into or out of that responsible set?

In the encounter, can a visitor tell which single line carries a part's belonging to the body before that line is removed — or does a circuit make every line on it dispensable, so that belonging is only learnable by cutting and seeing?

reconsider_if: The uncommitted placement changes: bridge_cut leaves AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation/map_data.json (currently the dirty working-tree entry "bridge_cut:0:0.95"), or the untracked artifact folder/registry file never lands in a commit — the record's premise that the artifact stands in this hall fails.

tutorial.md is dirty in the working tree; if its pending edits are reverted or rewritten so the bound excerpt stops being a verbatim contiguous byte substring, the tutorial passage binding must be re-selected and re-versioned.

A probe contradicts the hand arithmetic (e.g. component_count() != 2 at graph="tree", cut="bridge", closure="open", or _chord_edge != -1 at closure="open") — then the code reading in this record, not the artifact, is in question, and the fixture must be redone before any interpretation is trusted.

An encounter shows the plate text (STILL CONNECTED / BROKEN / NO BRIDGE TO CUT), not the removal-and-recolour, carries the meaning for visitors — then component_count() as the operationalization of 'the body's connected part' needs revision toward the verdict vocabulary.

The tree-for-body reading proves too loose: the hall's reroute concerns a named connection (edge 5, the left forearm) while _find_special always elects the first bridge (edge [0,1]); if that mismatch matters in the encounter, the mapping needs a bespoke graph value or a different operational route.
